body.statement:
For every fixed \(\kappa>0\), \(\mathcal M_n\cap\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}=\varnothing\): the uniform-shell condition places positive mass below every positive propensity threshold, whereas the uniform-overlap comparator imposes \(e(X)\ge\eta_-\) almost surely. For fixed \(n\) and \((r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\in[0,\bar r]^3\),
\[
\lim_{\kappa\to\infty}\rho_n=(1+r_{1n})n^{-1/2}+r_{1n}r_{en}+r_{0n}r_{en}\asymp n^{-1/2}+r_{1n}r_{en}+r_{0n}r_{en},
\]
uniformly under \(r_{1n}\le\bar r\). Writing the final rate form as \(C_n=n^{-1/2}+r_{0n}r_{en}+r_{1n}r_{en}\), the constant-weight Jin--Syrgkanis lower-bound template after its stated interpretive radius substitutions is \(J_n=n^{-1/2}+\max\{r_{0n},r_{1n}\}r_{en}\), and \(J_n\le C_n\le2J_n\). Separately, the Bonvini--Kennedy--Dukes--Balakrishnan one-functional template becomes only the treated-side form \(L_{1,n}=n^{-1/2}+r_{1n}r_{en}\le C_n\) under the purely interpretive substitution \(\varepsilon_n=r_{1n}\), \(\delta_n=r_{en}\); it supplies no control-side term. These are only algebraic source-class sanity comparisons: they prove neither a minimax equivalence for \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\) nor any class-inclusion transfer.
body.justification: This proposition proves strict separation of the shell and comparator classes and computes the exact fast-tail limit; its literature comparison is deliberately limited to algebraic lower-bound form.
body.gap: JinSyrgkanis2024StructureAgnosticDR, Theorem 1 and Remark 2, gives WATE lower bounds in its estimator-bounded source class, while BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024StructureAgnosticATE, Section 2, gives a one-functional lower rate in its pure structure-agnostic class. Neither citation proves a joint two-arm minimax equivalence for \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\).
body.consumer: Readers can verify class disjointness and the fast-tail algebraic sanity check without treating either cited lower-bound template as a transferred comparator theorem.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(\kappa>0\).  Suppose for contradiction that
\((P,m_0,m_1,p)\in\mathcal M_n\cap\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\), and set
\[
u_\star=\frac12\min\{\lambda_0,\eta_-\}.
\]
The declared ranges \(\lambda_0\in(0,1)\) and \(\eta_-\in(0,1)\) imply
\(0<u_\star\le\lambda_0\) and \(u_\star<\eta_-\).  By
\texttt{def:public-weak-overlap-class}, membership in \(\mathcal M_n\)
entails \texttt{ass:uniform-shell}.  Applying that assumption at
\(u_\star\) gives
\[
P\!\left\{\frac{u_\star}{2}<e(X)\le u_\star\right\}
\ge c_-u_\star^\kappa>0,
\]
where the strict inequality follows from \(c_->0\), \(u_\star>0\), and
\(\kappa>0\).  By \texttt{def:regular-overlap-class}, membership in
\(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\) entails
\texttt{ass:uniform-overlap-comparator}, and hence
\[
P\{e(X)\ge\eta_-\}=1.
\]
But \(u_\star<\eta_-\) implies
\[
\left\{\frac{u_\star}{2}<e(X)\le u_\star\right\}
\subseteq\{e(X)<\eta_-\},
\]
so the probability of the shell is zero.  This contradiction proves
\[
\mathcal M_n\cap\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}=\varnothing.
\]

Next fix \(n\in\mathbb N\) and
\((r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\in[0,\bar r]^3\).  In particular, \(n\ge1\) and
the three radii are nonnegative.  For every \(\kappa>1\),
\texttt{def:tail-noise-rate} gives
\[
Q_\kappa(n,r_{1n})=n^{-1/2}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\frac{\kappa}{2(\kappa+1)}\longrightarrow\frac12,
\qquad
\frac{\kappa}{\kappa+2}\longrightarrow1.
\]
Since \(n>0\), continuity of \(a\mapsto n^{-a}\) yields
\[
r_{1n}n^{-\kappa/[2(\kappa+1)]}
\longrightarrow r_{1n}n^{-1/2}.
\]
If \(r_{en}>0\), continuity of \(a\mapsto r_{en}^{a}\) gives
\(r_{en}^{\kappa/(\kappa+2)}\to r_{en}\).  If \(r_{en}=0\), then both
\(r_{en}^{\kappa/(\kappa+2)}\) and \(r_{en}\) equal zero because
\(\kappa/(\kappa+2)>0\).  Thus, in both cases,
\[
r_{1n}r_{en}^{\kappa/(\kappa+2)}
\longrightarrow r_{1n}r_{en}.
\]
Substitution into \texttt{def:sharp-rate} and passage to the limit in its
finite sum prove
\[
\lim_{\kappa\to\infty}\rho_n
=(1+r_{1n})n^{-1/2}+r_{1n}r_{en}+r_{0n}r_{en}.
\]

To verify the uniform comparison, define
\[
A_n=r_{1n}r_{en}+r_{0n}r_{en}\ge0,
\qquad
B_n=n^{-1/2}+A_n>0.
\]
Because \(0\le r_{1n}\le\bar r\),
\[
B_n
\le (1+r_{1n})n^{-1/2}+A_n
\le (1+\bar r)n^{-1/2}+A_n
\le (1+\bar r)B_n.
\]
The comparison constants \(1\) and \(1+\bar r\) are independent of \(n\)
and of the three radii.  Consequently,
\[
(1+r_{1n})n^{-1/2}+r_{1n}r_{en}+r_{0n}r_{en}
\asymp n^{-1/2}+r_{1n}r_{en}+r_{0n}r_{en}
\]
uniformly over \(r_{1n}\le\bar r\).

It remains to establish the two limited algebraic source comparisons.  Put
\[
C_n=n^{-1/2}+r_{0n}r_{en}+r_{1n}r_{en}.
\]
Under the purely interpretive substitutions in
\texttt{lem:jin-syrgkanis-regular-benchmark}, the constant-weight square-root
lower-bound form is
\[
J_n=n^{-1/2}+\max\{r_{0n},r_{1n}\}r_{en}.
\]
For nonnegative \(r_{0n}\), \(r_{1n}\), and \(r_{en}\),
\[
\max\{r_{0n},r_{1n}\}r_{en}
\le(r_{0n}+r_{1n})r_{en}
\le2\max\{r_{0n},r_{1n}\}r_{en}.
\]
Together with \(n^{-1/2}\le2n^{-1/2}\), these inequalities give
\[
J_n\le C_n\le2J_n.
\]

By \texttt{lem:bonvini-et-al-regular-benchmark}, the Bonvini--Kennedy--Dukes--Balakrishnan
citation concerns only one mean functional.  The treated-side interpretive
substitutions \(\varepsilon_n=r_{1n}\) and \(\delta_n=r_{en}\) give
\[
L_{1,n}=n^{-1/2}+r_{1n}r_{en}.
\]
Nonnegativity of \(r_{0n}r_{en}\) implies
\[
L_{1,n}\le C_n.
\]
No control-side expression or sum of two armwise lower bounds is used.  Both
cited results retain their own source classes and risk conventions, so neither
establishes a matching upper bound, a joint two-arm minimax equivalence for
\(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\), or a class-inclusion transfer.  This proves
exactly the stated algebraic sanity comparisons.
